newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at 35.89/90 vs dlr, seen flat.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at 35.89/90 vs dlr, seen flat.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.89/90 against the dollar on Thursday compared with the opening level of 35.91/93, dealers said on Thursday.
The rupee gained to 35.89/90 level within minutes of opening as a dollar inflow of over $50 million from Europe made its way into the market, a dealer at a foreign bank said.
Dollar demand from southern India, followed by bids by an influential Calcutta-based bank, helped the dollar recover in the afternoon session, dealers said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) also entered the frey, buying June, August and September dollars, they said.
"The market was briefly caught short," said a dealer. "They bought August and September dollars on higher spot basis," said the chief forex dealer at a city bank.
The rupee saw a high of 35.882 and a low of 35.920 on Thursday.

Forward dollar premiums edged down as exporters continued to sell dollars ahead of the fiscal year-end amid expectations that the RBI's monetary policy due in April will spur further cuts in interest rates, dealers said.
"Import cancellations and reversals continued to keep paying pressure at a low ebb," said a forward dealer.
The six-month annualised forward premium closed Thursday at 6.46 percent compared to the previous close of 6.69 percent.
Dealers had divergent views on how the rupee would fare in the new financial year beginning on April 1.
One dealer said he expected the rupee to continue at the current levels as far as he could see into the new year.
"I expect dollar inflows to continue at the current level and see RBI continuing to battle rupee's appreciation through its intervention.
Another dealer said if interest rates do come down as the RBI and government wants, the spot rupee has to weaken to help exporters.
